Theme

Latin word

ad

ad (+ accusative)

preposition with the accusative

at, by (beside a place); to the house of (going there); to, up to (a place or a person); towards, to

In this lexicon

  • at

    the recommended word · classical · Plaut. Amph. 1020–1021b: Quis ad forēs est?; Liv. 22.7.11: ad portās … multitūdō stetit

  • at the house of

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 4.4a.1: perbellē fēceris sī ad nōs vēneris

  • to

    the recommended word · classical · Ter. Ad. 970: ehō, accēde hūc ad mē; Cic. Fam. 9.4.1: tū sī minus ad nōs, nōs accurrēmus ad tē

  • towards

    the recommended word · classical · Mart. 14.172.1: ad tē reptantī … lacertae; Liv. 1.4.6: ad puerīlem vāgītum cursum flexisse

Examples

  • heus, ecquis hīc est? ecquis hoc aperit ōstium? — Quis ad forēs est? — Ego sum.

    Hey, is anybody here? Will somebody open this door? — Who’s at the door? — It’s me.Plaut. Amph. 1020–1021b

    In the entry for at

  • ad portās major prope mulierum quam virōrum multitūdō stetit, aut suōrum aliquem aut nūntiōs dē iīs opperiēns

    at the gates stood a crowd of women almost larger than the crowd of men, waiting for one of their own or for news of themLiv. 22.7.11

    In the entry for at

  • perbellē fēceris sī ad nōs vēneris

    it would be lovely of you to come to usCic. Att. 4.4a.1

    In the entry for at the house of

  • ehō, accēde hūc ad mē

    In the entry for to

    I’m off to the forum, unless you want somethingPlaut. Asin. 108

    In the entry for to

  • tū sī minus ad nōs, nōs accurrēmus ad tē

    if you don’t come to us, we will hurry to youCic. Fam. 9.4.1

    In the entry for to

  • Abī domum, ac deōs comprecāre ut uxōrem arcessās: abī.

    Go home and pray to the gods, so that you can fetch your bride: go!Ter. Ad. 699

    In the entry for to

    go home, my well-fed goats, the evening star is coming, goVerg. E. 10.77
